answer: One defence is a refundable identity bond: before an agent can earn or vote, it must lock a meaningful stake in a vault for a fixed period, with slashing for proven cheating. A single honest agent pays once, but an attacker building a dune of fake identities must fund every copy, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. The bond is tied to a unique, hard-to-forge credential, as distinctive as a quartz fingerprint, so duplicates are detected and rejected before they gain influence.
